findings.claim: The single-writer lock can be bypassed by a forked child using an inherited CaseLog. Reentrancy checks only the thread identifier, which is inherited by the calling thread across fork. The child enters without acquiring its own lock, so both processes can pass the same expected-position check and append duplicate sequence numbers.
findings.repro: On Linux, append entry 1 and enter log.writer() in the parent. Call os.fork() inside that context. In the child, call append on the inherited log with expected=1 while the parent still holds the context. The child can append instead of receiving CaseLocked. To expose the corruption, synchronize both processes at the start of _write, after both have verified position 1, then let both append. Both write entry 2.
